notes: Every caption has a stable ID. A recorded voice line can later be added as audio/<id>.mp3 and will play with the caption. {name}-style tokens are filled in by the game. {key:action} and {hold:action} show the player's own key for an action on screen, in brackets, and are left out of narration (see src/input/bindings.ts).

captions.egg.intro: An egg in the gravel. There is little an egg can do but wait. Cold water seeps between the stones.
captions.egg.hatch: Hatched. The alevin lives on its yolk sac, hidden in the gravel. Alevin turn to face into the current: it keeps them upright and keeps oxygen-rich water flowing over their gills.
captions.egg.flow: The flow is shifting. Turn to face into the current {key:steer} before it surges.
captions.egg.loosening: The current is working you loose. Face upstream and sink deeper into the gravel {key:dive}.
captions.egg.ready: The yolk is nearly gone. Swim up toward the light {hold:rise} and out of the gravel, ready to feed.
captions.egg.emerge: The fry wriggles up out of the stones and into open water. Only about 10 to 20 percent of eggs get this far.
captions.imprint.egg: Water seeps through the gravel, carrying the smell of this place. Young salmon are thought to learn the smell of home water. Facing into the flow, the alevin takes it in.
captions.imprint.fry: Water from home flows into the lake here. Lingering in it, the young fish keeps learning the smell of home.
captions.imprint.fryHint: A faint stream of drifting specks enters the lake near the weeds: water from home. Spend a little time in it to remember home better.
captions.imprint.smolt: Leaving is when the memory of home is thought to set most firmly. Swim calmly with the school, without panicking, and the smell of this river stays with you.
captions.fry.intro: The lake. Most sockeye spend one year here, some two, feeding on zooplankton.
captions.fry.controls: Click the water to steer with the mouse. Swim forward {key:forward}, burst {key:burst}, rise {key:rise} and dive {key:dive}. Swim through the glowing plankton to feed.
captions.fry.trout: A Dolly Varden has seen you. Rings in the water warn of a chase. The weeds at the shallow edge give cover.
captions.fry.safeWeeds: Hidden in the weeds. The Dolly Varden loses interest.
captions.fry.winter: Winter comes. Under the ice the fry grows slowly. Only about 5 to 10 percent of fry survive to leave the lake.
captions.smolt.intro: Spring. The young fish turns silver and leaves the lake at night, with thousands of others. Going together swamps the predators: they cannot eat everyone. Stay with the school.
captions.smolt.char: Char wait at the lake outlet. Rings in the water warn of a lunge. In a school, the char may take another fish instead of you.
captions.smolt.bird: A shadow on the surface: a diving bird. Go deep, or hide under the overhanging banks.
captions.smolt.merganser: A splash ahead: a merganser diving. It will chase underwater for a few seconds. Burst away.
captions.smolt.mouth: The river mouth, and the first taste of salt along the bottom. Gulls gather overhead and seals hunt the channel.
captions.estuary.enter: First light, and the estuary. River water is lighter than sea water: it slides out over the top, with the salt water below.
captions.estuary.edge: Brackish water, part river and part sea. Here, near the boundary between the layers, the young fish finishes adjusting to salt. Gulls and seals hunt here too.
captions.estuary.saltStress: Too salty, too soon. Its body is not ready yet, and holding its salt balance costs energy. Rise into fresher water, or push through.
captions.estuary.ready: Ready for the sea. A smolt's gills change to pump salt out instead of holding it in.
captions.smolt.gulls: Gulls, several at once. Watch every shadow.
captions.smolt.seal: Bubbles and a dark shape in the deep water: a seal. It will lunge straight. Swim across its path.
captions.smolt.nearMiss: Close. Back into the thick of the school: smolts go together to swamp their predators, which cannot take every fish.
captions.smolt.alone: You've left the school. A lone fish is the predators' only choice.
captions.smolt.salt: The open sea. Of the {total} smolts that left the lake beside you, {lost} were taken. Since it turned silver, its gills and kidneys have been readying it for salt water.
captions.ocean.intro: The North Pacific. Sockeye stay in the top 20 to 40 metres and do most of their growing here. Feed where the krill and small fish gather.
captions.ocean.orca: A dark shape at the edge of sight: an orca. It will charge in a straight line. Swim across its path, not away from it.
captions.ocean.revealJack: Something has changed. This male is maturing early, after a single year at sea. He will return small, about 300 millimetres: a jack. Jacks are rare: in a typical Bristol Bay run only 1 or 2 males in 100 do this.
captions.ocean.revealLarge: {years} years at sea in all. This male will return large, with a hooked jaw, big teeth and a hump.
captions.ocean.revealFemale: After {years} years at sea, she turns for home.
captions.return.intro: Coming home from the open sea. Nearing the coast, the salmon stops eating and lives on what it has stored.
captions.return.fatHint: The fat bar is all the fuel left for this life. Bursting burns it fast.
captions.return.netSlip: Small enough to slip through the mesh. Gillnets catch many returning sockeye, especially the larger males whose heads and teeth tangle, but jacks often slip through.
captions.return.pastNets: Past the nets. Find the river mouth that smells like home.
captions.return.bear: A shadow and a splash at the bank: a bear. Shallow riffles are where bears fish. Wait in a pool, or cross deep and fast.
captions.return.lowFat: Reserves are running low. Rest in the slower water near the banks.
captions.return.wrongBranch: The scent is fading. This branch is not home: back out and try the other.
captions.spawn.female: Judge the gravel by its cobble: too coarse is hard to dig, too fine and the eggs get less oxygen. Dig the redd {hold:act}, wait over it for a male, then cover the eggs {hold:act}. Drive off rival females with a burst {key:burst}.
captions.spawn.largeMale: Stay beside the female. When a rival comes, ram him side-on with a burst {key:burst} before he reaches her. Fights are quick, and size usually wins.
captions.spawn.jack: You are too small to fight. Settle into a hiding spot under the bank. When the big males clash, dart in beside the female {key:act}.
captions.spawn.digging: Digging. Sweeps of the tail lift the gravel and the current carries the fine silt away.
captions.spawn.needGravel: This spot is no good. Look for gravel of medium cobble.
captions.spawn.rivalFemale: Another female wants this spot. Charge her with a burst {key:burst}.
captions.spawn.rivalMale: A rival male is moving in. Ram him side-on with a burst {key:burst} before he reaches her.
captions.spawn.reddDisturbed: A rival dug into your redd.
captions.spawn.maleLost: A rival reached the female while you were away.
captions.spawn.femaleSpawned: The male joins you over the redd. The eggs are laid and fertilized.
captions.spawn.maleSpawned: The female releases her eggs and you fertilize them.
captions.spawn.jackWindow: The big males are fighting. Now!
captions.spawn.jackSuccess: In and out before the guard noticed. Sneakers can fertilize some of the eggs, though usually fewer than a guarding male.
captions.spawn.jackChased: The guarding male drove you off. Wait for an opening.
captions.death.yolk: The yolk ran out before the alevin left the gravel. An alevin has to swim up and start feeding before its stored food is gone.
captions.death.scour: Washed out. A surge of water tore the alevin from the gravel. High flows that scour the gravel kill many eggs and alevin before they ever emerge.
captions.death.trout: Taken by a Dolly Varden. Trout and Dolly Varden are the main predators of fry in the lake.
captions.death.bird: Taken by a diving bird. Smolts near the surface are easy targets for mergansers and gulls.
captions.death.gull: Taken by a gull. Birds take more smolts as they near the sea, where the gulls gather.
captions.death.char: Taken by a char at the lake outlet. Larger fish gather where the smolts leave the lake.
captions.death.merganser: Taken by a merganser. These diving ducks chase smolts underwater.
captions.death.seal: Taken by a seal. Seals gather at river mouths when the smolts run, and hunt salmon throughout their years at sea.
captions.death.gillnet: Caught in a gillnet. The fish swims in, its head and teeth tangle, and it cannot back out. Larger males are caught most.
captions.death.bear: Taken by a bear. Bears feed most easily in shallow creeks. They take males first, then large females.
captions.death.exhaustion: Exhausted. Returning salmon do not eat, and this one ran out of stored energy before reaching home.
captions.death.noSpawn: Spawning failed. The season ended before this fish could spawn.
captions.end.decay: Like other Pacific salmon, a sockeye dies after spawning.
captions.end.forest: Its body feeds the stream, the insects, the bears and the trees along the bank.
captions.end.hatch: Under the gravel, the next generation is already growing.
captions.end.spentFemale: Spent, she guards the redd for as long as she can. Females live several weeks after spawning, rarely more than a month.
captions.end.spentMale: Spawned out, he grows sluggish and ragged on the grounds.
captions.end.carcass: The body settles among the stones and slowly breaks down.
captions.end.seasons: Autumn turns to winter, and winter to spring.
captions.egg.floodComing: The water is rising and clouding with silt. A flood is coming. Face into the current {key:steer} and get down deep in the gravel {key:dive}.
captions.egg.flood: The flood. High water tears at the gravel and scours the redd. Stay deep and keep facing upstream.
captions.egg.floodOver: The flood passes. Of the {total} alevin hatched around you, {lost} were torn out of the gravel. Scouring floods are the main killer of eggs and alevin.
captions.egg.tooEarly: Not yet. Higher in the gravel the surges hit harder. Rise when the yolk is nearly used.
captions.ocean.shark: A fast grey shape below: a salmon shark. It will strike in a straight line. Swim across its path.
captions.ocean.yearsAtSea: Each extra year at sea brings more growth, and more risk: perhaps half of fish survive each later year. Jacks avoid this by returning early.
captions.ocean.crowded: A crowded year at sea. Pink salmon are abundant every other year, and sockeye grow less when they compete for food.
captions.death.sea: Lost at sea during a later year: orcas, salmon sharks or seals. Perhaps half of fish survive each extra year. Jacks, returning after one year, skip this risk.
captions.return.heat: A warm, low-water year. Heat stress and low oxygen kill fish before they spawn. Rest in the deeper, cooler pools.
captions.return.coolSeep: Cold water, seeping up through the gravel. In a warm year, cool pockets like this let a salmon wait out the heat. Rest here and the strain eases, but every minute still burns fat.
captions.return.coolPool: Cooler water in the deep pool. Rest near the bottom and let the heat stress ease, then push on before the fat runs low.
captions.return.heatStress: The water is too warm and short of oxygen. Heat stress is building. Find deeper, cooler water and rest.
captions.death.heat: Killed by heat stress. Warm, low water holds less oxygen, and salmon that spend too long in it die before they spawn.
captions.return.track: At sea, salmon navigate by the Earth's magnetic field. Feel for it: faint shimmering marks appear ahead when you are on the track. If they fade, sweep side to side until you find them again.
captions.return.lostTrack: The pull has faded. You've drifted off the track. Sweep across until the shimmer returns.
captions.return.overshoot: The coast. This doesn't feel like the right mouth. Overshooting is one of the commonest mistakes; turn back along the shore.
captions.return.wrongRiver: This river doesn't smell like home. Salmon test a river and back out when it is wrong. Turn around.
captions.return.rightRiver: The smell of home. This is the river.
captions.return.scent.strong: Fresh water ahead. The smell of home comes through clearly and steadily: this fish learned it well.
captions.return.scent.fair: Fresh water ahead. Somewhere in it is the smell of home, faint but there.
captions.return.scent.weak: Fresh water ahead. The smell of home is faint and patchy: this fish learned it poorly, and other rivers smell much the same.
captions.return.strayScent: This river smells almost like home. A fish that learned home poorly can easily stray into the wrong one.
captions.return.strayScentClear: This river smells of fresh water, but not of home. The smell fades quickly up the channel.
captions.spawn.cobbleLarge: Coarse cobble. It is hard work to dig, and the redd will be poor.
captions.spawn.cobbleSmall: Fine gravel. Easy to dig, but the eggs will get less oxygen.
captions.spawn.fightWonSide: Side-on, mouth open: he gave way. Size usually wins, but timing and position helped.
captions.spawn.fightLost: He was bigger, and you were driven off. Hit rivals side-on, before they reach her.
captions.spawn.bear: A bear wades into the shallows. Bears take the biggest males first, then large females, and small jacks last. Watch for its shadow.
captions.spawn.bearTookGuard: The bear took the guarding male.
captions.spawn.bearEats: The bear carries its catch up the bank to eat, then walks the bank again.
captions.spawn.bearPartial: A big run. When salmon are plentiful, bears often eat only part of each fish and go back for another.
captions.spawn.scavengers: Gulls and eagles come for what the bears leave.
captions.spawn.jackScarce: Too many jacks, too few hiding spots. They fight each other for the cover under the bank.
captions.spawn.jackSpotTaken: Another jack holds this hiding spot. Charge him out with a burst {key:burst}, or find another.
captions.spawn.jackSpotWon: You pushed him out of the spot.
captions.spawn.jackEvicted: Another jack pushed you out of your hiding spot.
captions.spawn.habitat.creek: A small creek: shallow water and undercut banks. Bears catch fish most easily in creeks, and the bank cover gives jacks places to hide.
captions.spawn.habitat.river: A river: deeper, faster water over coarse gravel. River sockeye are larger and deeper-bodied than creek fish, and bears find them harder to catch.
captions.spawn.habitat.beach: A lake beach: still water along the shore. Beach spawners are the largest and deepest-bodied sockeye. Bears catch fish less easily here than in creeks, and there are few places for jacks to hide.
captions.spawn.jackBeach: You are too small to fight. Hide behind a boulder, the only cover on the beach. When the big males clash, dart in beside the female {key:act}.
captions.spawn.reddReady: The redd is dug. Stay over it and wait for a male.
captions.spawn.maleArrives: A male has joined you. He stays close while you dig.
captions.spawn.femaleChoice: Two males fight beside your redd. Fights are quick and mostly settled by size, and you will spawn with the winner.
captions.spawn.waitMale: The redd is ready, but no male is beside it. Wait over it.
captions.spawn.bury: Now cover the eggs: sweep gravel over them with your tail {hold:act} over the redd.
captions.spawn.buried: The eggs are covered. Guard the redd against other females for as long as your strength lasts.
captions.spawn.superimposed: Another female dug into your redd, and some of your eggs were dug up. Drive rivals off with a burst {key:burst}.
captions.spawn.senescence: Your strength is fading, and here it will not come back. After weeks on the spawning grounds, salmon turn sluggish and ragged.
captions.spawn.spentFemale: Your strength is gone. You guarded the redd for as long as you could. Females live several weeks after spawning, rarely more than a month.
captions.spawn.spentMale: Your strength is gone. Like other Pacific salmon, a sockeye dies after spawning.
captions.spawn.spentJack: Your strength is gone, and the season is over.
captions.spawn.femaleReady: She is ready to spawn. Get beside her, now.
captions.spawn.secondFemale: A second female has started to dig farther along the bed. In the game you can go to her or stay with the first; leaving costs strength and draws more bears.
captions.spawn.maleLeaves: You leave her to look for another female.
captions.spawn.maleSpawnedAgain: The second female releases her eggs and you fertilize them.
captions.spawn.secondLost: She spawned with another male before you reached her.
captions.spawn.jackCommon: Many jacks on the grounds this year: in the game, more of them compete for every opening, and each sneak is worth less.
captions.spawn.jackRare: Few jacks on the grounds this year: in the game, less competition for the openings, and each sneak is worth more.
captions.year.warm: A warm year. This year favours early-run fish. Late-run fish burn more fat on the way home.
captions.year.highWater: High water. This year, early-run and deep-bodied fish struggle more against the flow.
captions.year.lowWater: Low water. This year, deep-bodied fish are easier for bears to reach in the shallows.
captions.year.bigRun: A big run. More big males crowd the spawning grounds: harder for large males, more fights and openings for jacks.
captions.year.smallRun: A small run. Fewer rivals on the spawning grounds, which suits large males and leaves jacks fewer openings.
captions.year.crowded: A crowded ocean. Fish grow less at sea and come home smaller.
captions.year.ordinary: An ordinary year. No trait has a clear advantage.
captions.pop.lakeCrowded: Your parents spawned in a big run. Their carcasses fed the lake, but this year it is crowded with fry, and the plankton is shared thinly.
captions.pop.lakeRoomy: Your parents' run was small. Fewer carcasses fed the lake, but there are fewer fry to share it, so the plankton goes further.
captions.pop.lakeOrdinary: An ordinary number of fry share the lake this year.
captions.pop.fisheryHeavy: A big run is coming home. The fishery is managed to let enough fish through to spawn, and takes more of the rest: more nets on the approach.
captions.pop.fisheryLight: A small run is coming home. The fishery holds back so enough fish reach the spawning grounds: fewer nets on the approach.
captions.pop.fisheryClosed: The run is too small to fish. The fishery stays closed so that enough fish reach the spawning grounds: no nets this year.
captions.pop.fisheryOrdinary: The fishery takes what it can spare above the number of fish it lets through to spawn: the usual nets on the approach.
captions.pop.runHistory: The river's run rises and falls. Many spawners mean many young, but a crowded lake and gravel give each fewer chances; a few spawners can rebuild a run. One fish's success hardly moves it.
captions.year.betHedging: Every year favours different fish. Over many years, a population that keeps its variety does better than one that bets on a single strategy.
captions.lineage.traitDrift: Each panel shows the inherited part of a trait, averaged over the brood each fish was chosen from. Zero is the home population's average. The offspring you pick, the mates they meet, strays and chance all move it.
captions.offspring.intro: Each bar shows what this fish inherited, against the average fish of your river. The coming year rewards some traits and punishes others, and next year may turn it around.
captions.offspring.fit.warm.runTiming.good: Inclined to run early, ahead of the warmest water: less fat burned on the way home in a warm year.
captions.offspring.fit.warm.runTiming.poor: Inclined to run late, into warmer water: more fat burned on the way home in a warm year.
captions.offspring.fit.cool.runTiming.good: Inclined to run late, which a cool year favours: less fat burned on the way home.
captions.offspring.fit.cool.runTiming.poor: Inclined to run early, while a cool year favours later fish.
captions.offspring.fit.highWater.runTiming.good: Inclined to run late, missing the worst of the high water.
captions.offspring.fit.highWater.runTiming.poor: Inclined to run early, into the high water: harder going against the flow.
captions.offspring.fit.highWater.bodyDepth.poor: Deep-bodied: harder work against the flow in high water.
captions.offspring.fit.lowWater.bodyDepth.poor: Deep-bodied: easier for bears to reach in the shallows of a low-water year.
captions.offspring.fit.bigRun.jack.good: Leans toward the jack strategy, which finds more openings in a big run.
captions.offspring.fit.bigRun.jack.poor: Likely to grow into a large male, and a big run brings more rivals to fight.
captions.offspring.fit.smallRun.jack.good: Likely to grow into a large male, and a small run means fewer rivals.
captions.offspring.fit.smallRun.jack.poor: Leans toward the jack strategy, while a small run leaves jacks fewer openings.
captions.offspring.fit.ordinary: No trait has a clear advantage in the coming year.
captions.offspring.fit.neutral: Close to the river's average in the traits the coming year rewards or punishes.
captions.recap.fit.ordinary: No trait had a clear advantage this year.
captions.recap.fit.neutral: Close to the river's average in the traits this year rewarded or punished.
captions.recap.mapNote: The route of this life. Crosses mark where fish of the brood died; the bar below counts the years.
captions.lineage.extinct: The whole brood died before any of them could spawn. Nothing of this line returns to the gravel.
captions.lineage.strayOffer: Salmon sometimes stray from the stream they were born in. A stray that has joined this river can start a new line here.
captions.year.cool: A cool year. This year favours late-run fish, which burn less fat on the way home.
captions.return.angler: A flash in the pool: an angler's lure swinging across the current. Give it a wide berth.
captions.return.hooked: Hooked! Burst again and again {key:burst} to tear free before the line wins.
captions.return.unhooked: Free. The hook tore loose, but the fight cost precious fat.
captions.return.migrants: Other sockeye from this river are coming home too. They travel with you, hold in the pools and try the falls alongside you.
captions.return.migrantTaken: The bear took one of the others. In company, each fish is a little safer.
captions.return.rapids: Rapids. The current is strong and uneven. Dash from rock to rock: the slack water behind each boulder is a place to rest.
captions.return.eddy: Slack water behind the boulder. Rest here to get your breath back before the next dash.
captions.return.falls: A falls. Salmon leap them from the pool below. Build up speed, then burst and rise together {key:burst} {key:rise} just under the surface. Launch from the standing wave, below the low step where the water pours thickest.
captions.return.firstLeap: Over the falls! Salmon can clear falls like this by leaping from the pool below, but every hard effort burns reserves they cannot replace.
captions.return.leapFail: Not enough. The falling water knocks the fish back into the pool. Rest, then build more speed, and launch from the standing wave below the low step.
captions.return.sideChannel: A lower side channel along the bank is open now. It is a longer climb up small steps against fast water, and it costs fat, but it gets past the falls.
captions.return.chuteUp: Up the side channel and past the falls, at a cost in fat.
captions.return.lake.enter: The river opens into the lake where this fish grew up. One of the streams that feed it is home.
captions.return.lake.enterBeach: The river opens into the lake where this fish grew up. Somewhere along its shore is the beach where it hatched.
captions.return.lake.wait: Not ready to spawn yet. Wait in the lake while the spawning colours come on, and follow the smell of home across it.
captions.return.lake.warm: A warm year. The top of the lake is warm, and cooler water lies deeper down. Wait deep.
captions.return.lake.coolDeep: Cool water below the warm top layer. Wait here and the heat stress eases, though every minute still burns fat.
captions.return.lake.ready: The spawning colours have come on. Ready: go home.
captions.return.lake.notReady: Home, but not ready to spawn yet. Wait in deeper water, out of the bears' reach.
captions.return.lake.wrongInflow: This stream smells of fresh water, but not of home. Back out and try another.
captions.return.lake.wrongBeach: Not this beach. The smell of home comes from somewhere else along the shore.
captions.return.lake.lostScent: The smell of home has thinned out in the open lake. Sweep across until you find it again.
captions.return.lake.bear: A bear in the shallows. Bears fish the stream mouths and beaches; deep water is out of reach.
captions.return.arriveBeach: The beach where this fish hatched, at the end of the crossing. Home.
captions.death.angler: Landed by an angler. Sport fishing takes returning salmon in the rivers, as the commercial nets do on the approach.
captions.fry.lesson: Early summer, at the weed edge. Watch for rings spreading through the water: they mean a Dolly Varden is about to chase. When you see them, dart into the weeds.
captions.fry.lessonDone: Well read. Food in the open is worth having, but only with cover close by.
captions.fry.dusk: Dusk. As the light fades, the plankton rises toward the surface. The best feeding of the day is up high, in the half-light, while hunters see less.
captions.fry.winterHint: The water is cold and food is scarce. Every burst spends reserves you cannot easily replace. Rest when you can: ease off {key:forward} and take only the food that drifts close.
captions.fry.starving: The reserves are gone, and the fry is burning its own growth to stay alive. Rest, and find food.
captions.fry.decide: About 6 in 10 sockeye leave the lake after one year. Follow the drifting current to the outlet to leave now, or wait in the weeds to stay another year: a bigger fish when it leaves, but another year among the predators.
captions.fry.decideGrown: This fry grew well this year.
captions.fry.decideSmall: This fry grew slowly this year. Another year in the lake would make it bigger when it leaves.
captions.fry.secondSummer: A second summer in the lake.
captions.fry.second: Bigger now, but the predators are still here. Deep by day, up at dusk and dawn.
captions.fry.secondWinter: Another winter passes under the ice.
captions.fry.leave: After one year in the lake, like most sockeye, the young fish follows the current toward the outlet.
captions.fry.leaveSecond: After two years in the lake, a bigger young fish follows the current toward the outlet.
captions.fry.day: Daylight. The plankton has sunk into deep, cold water, and young sockeye go down after it. Near the surface and over the shallows a fry is easy to see.
captions.fry.dayAgain: Day again. Back down into the dark.
captions.fry.night: Night. Too dark to see much food, and too dark for most hunters to see you.
captions.fry.dawn: Dawn. The plankton is still high. Feed once more before it sinks with the daylight.
captions.fry.warm: The water up here is warm, and warm water burns through what you have eaten. Down in the cold, a fry spends less.
captions.fry.charDeep: Dolly Varden hunt the deep water by day too, but in the dark they must come close to see you.
captions.fry.merganser: A merganser on the surface. Dive deep, below where it can follow.
captions.fry.mergDeep: Too deep for the merganser. It gives up.
captions.fry.charLost: Lost in the dark water. The Dolly Varden gives up.
captions.ocean.skipOrca: Weeks later, farther out. Another patch of food, and something large is hunting here too.
captions.ocean.skipSeal: Feeding near the surface. Seals and sea lions hunt salmon throughout their years at sea.
captions.ocean.seal: Bubbles and a dark shape: a seal. It lunges at where you are going, so turn hard as it comes.
captions.ocean.pinks: Pink salmon everywhere, all after the same food. Get to it first.
captions.ocean.pinksGone: A lean season: less food for every fish.
captions.ocean.skipShark: Months pass. Deeper water, and something fast below.
captions.ocean.autumnMale: For a male, this is thought to be when his path is set. His genes, and how fast he has grown, decide whether he matures early.
captions.egg.intro.short: An egg in the gravel. Cold water seeps between the stones.
captions.egg.hatch.short: Hatched. The alevin lives on its yolk sac, hidden in the gravel.
captions.egg.floodComing.short: The water is rising and clouding with silt. A flood is coming: get down deep {key:dive}.
captions.egg.floodOver.short: The flood passes. Of the {total} alevin hatched around you, {lost} were torn out.
captions.imprint.egg.short: Water seeping through the gravel carries the smell of this place.
captions.imprint.fryHint.short: Water from home drifts into the lake near the weeds. Linger in it to remember home.
captions.imprint.smolt.short: Leaving is when the memory of home is thought to set. Swim calmly, without panicking.
captions.fry.controls.short: Swim through the glowing plankton to feed.
captions.fry.lesson.short: Early summer at the weed edge. When rings spread through the water, dart into the weeds.
captions.fry.dusk.short: Dusk. The plankton rises: feed up high in the half-light.
captions.fry.winterHint.short: Cold water and scarce food. Rest when you can, and take only the food that drifts close.
captions.fry.decide.short: About 6 in 10 sockeye leave after one year. Follow the current out, or wait in the weeds.
captions.fry.day.short: Daylight. The plankton has sunk into deep, cold water. Go down after it.
captions.fry.warm.short: Warm water burns through what you have eaten. The cold deep costs less.
captions.smolt.intro.short: Spring. The young fish turns silver and leaves the lake at night, with thousands of others.
captions.smolt.char.short: Char wait at the lake outlet. Rings in the water warn of a lunge.
captions.smolt.nearMiss.short: Close. Back into the thick of the school.
captions.smolt.salt.short: The open sea. Of the {total} smolts that left the lake beside you, {lost} were taken.
captions.estuary.edge.short: Brackish water. Near the boundary between the layers, it finishes adjusting to salt.
captions.estuary.saltStress.short: Too salty, too soon: it costs energy. Rise into fresher water, or push through.
captions.estuary.enter.short: First light, and the estuary. Fresher river water slides out over the salt water below.
captions.ocean.intro.short: The North Pacific. Sockeye do most of their growing here. Feed where the food gathers.
captions.ocean.revealJack.short: Something has changed. This male is maturing early, after a single year at sea: a jack.
captions.ocean.yearsAtSea.short: Each extra year at sea brings more growth, and more risk.
captions.ocean.crowded.short: A crowded year at sea. Sockeye grow less when they compete with pink salmon for food.
captions.ocean.autumnMale.short: For a male, this is thought to be when his path is set.
captions.return.netSlip.short: Small enough to slip through the mesh. Jacks often slip through.
captions.return.bear.short: A shadow and a splash at the bank: a bear. Wait in a pool, or cross deep and fast.
captions.return.heat.short: A warm, low-water year. Rest in the deeper, cooler pools.
captions.return.coolSeep.short: Cold water, seeping up through the gravel. Rest here and the strain eases.
captions.return.coolPool.short: Cooler water in the deep pool. Rest near the bottom, then push on.
captions.return.track.short: At sea, salmon navigate by the Earth's magnetic field. Faint shimmering marks show the track.
captions.return.overshoot.short: The coast, but this doesn't feel like the right mouth. Turn back along the shore.
captions.return.scent.weak.short: Fresh water ahead. The smell of home is faint and patchy.
captions.return.migrants.short: Other sockeye from this river are coming home too.
captions.return.rapids.short: Rapids. Dash from rock to rock, and rest in the slack water behind each boulder.
captions.return.falls.short: A falls. Build up speed, then burst and rise together {key:burst} {key:rise} from the standing wave.
captions.return.firstLeap.short: Over the falls! But every hard effort burns reserves the fish cannot replace.
captions.return.leapFail.short: Not enough. Rest, then build more speed and launch from the standing wave.
captions.return.sideChannel.short: A lower side channel along the bank is open now. It costs fat, but it gets past the falls.
captions.return.lake.wait.short: Not ready to spawn yet. Wait in the lake while the colours come on.
captions.return.lake.enterBeach.short: The lake where this fish grew up. Somewhere along its shore is home.
captions.return.lake.coolDeep.short: Cool water below the warm top layer. Wait here and the heat stress eases.
captions.return.lake.bear.short: A bear in the shallows. Deep water is out of reach.
captions.spawn.female.short: Find gravel of medium cobble and dig the redd {hold:act}.
captions.spawn.largeMale.short: Stay beside the female. Ram rivals side-on with a burst {key:burst}.
captions.spawn.jack.short: Too small to fight. Hide under the bank, and dart in {key:act} when the big males clash.
captions.spawn.jackBeach.short: Too small to fight. Hide behind a boulder, and dart in {key:act} when the big males clash.
captions.spawn.jackSuccess.short: In and out before the guard noticed.
captions.spawn.bear.short: A bear wades into the shallows. Bears take the biggest males first.
captions.spawn.habitat.creek.short: A small creek: shallow water and undercut banks.
captions.spawn.habitat.river.short: A river: deeper, faster water over coarse gravel.
captions.spawn.habitat.beach.short: A lake beach: still water along the shore.
captions.spawn.femaleChoice.short: Two males fight beside your redd. You will spawn with the winner.
captions.spawn.superimposed.short: Another female dug into your redd. Drive rivals off with a burst {key:burst}.
captions.spawn.senescence.short: Your strength is fading, and here it will not come back.
captions.spawn.spentFemale.short: Your strength is gone. You guarded the redd for as long as you could.
captions.spawn.secondFemale.short: A second female is digging farther along. Go to her, or stay with the first.
captions.spawn.jackCommon.short: Many jacks this year: in the game, each sneak is worth less.
captions.spawn.jackRare.short: Few jacks this year: in the game, each sneak is worth more.
captions.spawn.crowdBig: A big run: the gravel is crowded with pairs and redds, and later with the dead. In the game, crowded grounds bring more rivals and more openings, and give the bear more fish to choose from.
captions.spawn.crowdSmall: A small run: only a few pairs on the gravel this year. In the game, fewer rivals and fewer openings, and the bear has fewer fish to choose from.
captions.spawn.crowdReddTaken: Another female's redd is here. Find open gravel.
captions.spawn.patchContested: Good gravel. In the game, good patches draw more females wanting the same spot, so expect to defend it.
captions.spawn.crowdOpening: Males are clashing over another pair close by. That is an opening too.
captions.spawn.charEggs: A char is after the loose eggs. Charge it off {key:burst}, and cover the eggs {hold:act}.
captions.spawn.charDriven: The char backs off, for now.
captions.spawn.eggsSafe: Covered. In the game, buried eggs are out of the thieves' reach.
captions.spawn.gullEggs: A gull has come down over this shallow redd to pick at loose eggs. In the game it can't be chased off: only covering the eggs {hold:act} stops it.
captions.spawn.crowdBig.short: A big run: the gravel is crowded with pairs and redds.
captions.spawn.crowdSmall.short: A small run: only a few pairs on the gravel this year.
captions.spawn.patchContested.short: Good gravel draws other females. Expect to defend it.
captions.spawn.gullEggs.short: A gull is picking at loose eggs. Cover them {hold:act}.
captions.card.pop.lakeCrowded: A crowded lake: the plankton is shared thinly.
captions.card.pop.lakeRoomy: Few fry in the lake, so the plankton goes further.
captions.card.pop.fisheryClosed: The fishery is closed: no nets.
captions.help.mouseLock: The mouse now steers: move it to turn, and to tilt up or down. To get the pointer back, pause {key:pause}.
captions.ocean.orca.short: A dark shape at the edge of sight: an orca. Swim across its path, not away from it.
